_about: Golden questions for search_guidelines. Each expected page was checked by reading the extracted page text on 2026-09-24 (the 'evidence' field says what is on the page, without quoting it, to keep lane B and C text out of the repository). A hit is a returned passage from the expected document on one of the expected PDF pages (or, for the ADWG web page, in one of the expected sections). Out-of-scope questions must return 'not covered'. 'expects_numeric_note' marks questions that ask for a value, where the lookup_limit note must appear; for the others the note is not checked. One expected page was added after reviewing search output (g02, marked added_after_review); every other expectation was set before running the search. Group 'practitioner' (p01 to p07, added 2026-09-24): questions a practitioner asked while testing the search; the expected pages were set by reading the extracted text before the search was changed, and the same questions were used to tune the search, so they are not a held-out test. Group 'casual' (c01 to c12, added 2026-09-24): everyday wordings of in-scope questions and chatty off-topic ones, written after held-out set 1 showed that casual questions were refused; their expected pages were set by reading the extracted text, and they were used to tune the search.
corpus: nepm-b1, nemp-3.0, dwer-amcs, dwer-irc, adwg-pfas (nemp-3.1 not indexed: host unreachable)

in_scope.question: What is the health investigation level for lead in residential soil with a garden (HIL A)?
in_scope.evidence: Table 1A(1) with the lead row (printed p. 48, PDF p. 56) and the table notes defining HIL A (printed p. 49, PDF p. 57).

in_scope.question: Where do the groundwater investigation levels for drinking water come from?
in_scope.evidence: Section 2.8 says GILs are based on the ADWG (PDF p. 25); Table 1C has the drinking water column (PDF p. 74) and footnote B naming the ADWG (PDF p. 81). Added after reviewing a search run: DWER-AMCS section 11 says the drinking water assessment levels are derived from NHMRC and NRMMC 2011 (printed p. 68, PDF p. 73).

in_scope.question: How is an ecological investigation level calculated from the added contaminant limit and the ambient background concentration?
in_scope.evidence: Section 2.5 introduces EILs, ACL and ABC (PDF p. 21); 2.5.8 defines the ACL (PDF p. 22); the worked example sums ABC and ACL (PDF p. 52).

in_scope.question: What are the limitations of the petroleum health screening levels?
in_scope.evidence: Section 2.4.13 Limitations of the HSLs (PDF p. 20); section 2.4.1 tells professionals to know the HSL limitations (PDF p. 14).

in_scope.question: Which soil textures were the petroleum HSLs developed for?
in_scope.evidence: Section 2.4.7 Soil texture: HSLs developed for sand, silt and clay (PDF p. 17). Petroleum screening is outside Evidenceline's checks, so a scope note is expected.

in_scope.question: What is the NEMP 3.0 drinking water guideline for the sum of PFOS and PFHxS?
in_scope.evidence: Table 4 Health-based guideline values developed by health authorities, drinking water row (printed p. 48, PDF p. 57).

in_scope.question: What does the PFAS NEMP say about using the total oxidisable precursor assay?
in_scope.evidence: Section 19 analysis methods: the TOP assay row of the methods table (PDF p. 187), 19.1.1 to 19.3 on TOP and TOF assays (PDF pp. 188 to 193).

in_scope.question: What is the freshwater 99% species protection value for PFOS?
in_scope.evidence: Table 8 Ecological water quality guideline values, freshwater 99% species protection row (PDF p. 68).

in_scope.question: Can PFAS-contaminated soil be reused on another site?
in_scope.evidence: Section 12 Reuse of PFAS-contaminated materials: 12.1 Reuse of soil, decision tree and detailed risk assessment (PDF pp. 115 to 119).

in_scope.question: Which PFAS are listed under the Stockholm Convention?
in_scope.evidence: Section 2.1: the PFAS listed as persistent organic pollutants under the Stockholm Convention (PDF pp. 19 and 20).

in_scope.question: What is the drinking water guideline for PFBS?
in_scope.evidence: ADWG PFAS fact sheet, Guideline section (PFBS statement) and the PFBS derivation subsection.

in_scope.question: How are PFAS measured in water samples in the laboratory?
in_scope.evidence: ADWG PFAS fact sheet, Measurement section; NEMP 3.0 19.1.1 Standard methods (PDF p. 188).

in_scope.question: How can PFAS be removed from drinking water by treatment?
in_scope.evidence: ADWG PFAS fact sheet, Treatment of drinking water section.

in_scope.question: What must a detailed site investigation report include according to the DWER reporting checklist?
in_scope.evidence: Appendix A, Table A1 Reporting checklist for PSI and DSI reports (PDF pp. 111 and 112).

in_scope.question: What triggers a site assessment?
in_scope.evidence: Section 6.1 Triggers for site assessment (printed p. 15, PDF p. 20).

in_scope.question: Which older contaminated sites guidelines have been superseded?
in_scope.evidence: Section 2 Introduction lists the superseded contaminated sites management series (printed p. 3, PDF p. 8).

in_scope.question: What should a sampling and analysis quality plan include?
in_scope.evidence: Section 9.2 Sampling and analysis quality plans (PDF p. 36) and 9.3 on what the SAQP should demonstrate (PDF p. 37).

in_scope.question: Which industries and land uses are potentially contaminating?
in_scope.evidence: Section 8.2 Potentially contaminating activities (PDF p. 31) and Appendix B Potentially contaminating industries, activities and land uses (PDF pp. 139 and 140).

in_scope.question: How long do I have to report a known contaminated site to DWER?
in_scope.evidence: Section 6.4 Timeframes for reporting: known contamination within 21 days (PDF p. 32); section 5.3 refers to the 21-day duty (PDF p. 19).

in_scope.question: What are the seven site classifications under the Contaminated Sites Act?
in_scope.evidence: Table 2 Site classifications under the CS Act (PDF p. 15, continued p. 16) and the classification table in section 7 (PDF p. 34).

in_scope.question: When is a memorial registered on the certificate of title?
in_scope.evidence: Section 7.7 Memorials on certificates of title (PDF p. 46) and 7.10 Summary of restrictions on use and memorials (PDF p. 50).

in_scope.question: How should asbestos found in soil be reported?
in_scope.evidence: Section 5.5 Asbestos contamination (PDF p. 24).

in_scope.question: How should PFAS samples be stored and what containers should be used?
in_scope.evidence: Section 18.2.1: polypropylene or HDPE sample containers, not glass with lined lids (PDF pp. 171 to 173); Appendix B.3.6 Collecting samples: laboratory-supplied bottles, double bags, on ice or in a fridge below 4 C (PDF pp. 226 to 228).

in_scope.question: What is the ecological soil value for PFOS?
in_scope.evidence: Section 8.7.1 Ecological soil guideline values, direct and indirect exposure (PDF pp. 63 and 64) and Table 6 Ecological guideline values for soil (PDF p. 65).

in_scope.question: How many soil samples are needed for a site of one hectare?
in_scope.evidence: Section 9.4, box 'Minimum number of samples': no minimum number of sampling points is recommended for a given size of site; the number follows from the CSM and the DQOs (PDF p. 38). No indexed document gives a number per hectare.

in_scope.question: How long after installing a monitoring well should I wait before sampling groundwater?
in_scope.evidence: No indexed document states a waiting time. The closest guidance: section 18.2.1 Groundwater, well development for PFAS (PDF pp. 172 and 173), and Appendix B.3.6, purge until parameters are stable before sampling (PDF pp. 227 and 228).

in_scope.question: What should a DSI report contain?
in_scope.evidence: Appendix A, Table A1 Reporting checklist for PSI and DSI reports (PDF pp. 111 and 112).

in_scope.question: What is a conceptual site model?
in_scope.evidence: Section 7 Conceptual site model, 7.1 Overview: what a CSM describes and that it is iterative (PDF pp. 27 and 28).

in_scope.question: When do I have to report contamination to DWER?
in_scope.evidence: Section 6.1 persons with a duty to report (PDF p. 25); 6.4 Timeframes for reporting, Table 8: known contamination within 21 days, suspected as soon as reasonably practicable (PDF p. 32); 5.3 refers to the 21-day duty (PDF p. 19).
